To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

• the creep free analysis of steel structures can be performed using a modified Eurocode 4 material model; • the creep free material model for steel can be applied in a general fire analysis; • the creep strain is a function of the temperature and the time of exposure; • the creep rate increases as the temperature rises; • the creep strains are not significant at temperatures lower than 300°C; • the creep effect on the steel material is more pronounced at high temperatures (above 300°C);
creep free analysis can be performed with the proposed modified Eurocode 2 carbon steel material model.
creep free fire analysis of simply supported steel members can be performed by using a modified Eurocode 2 steel material model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the creep free fire analysis of simply supported steel structures with the Eurocode 2 and Eurocode 3 models.
the development of a methodology for creep free fire analysis of structures.
the creep free analysis of structural steel members.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Eurocode 4 steel material model is a reasonable and reliable material model for creep analysis of steel structures.
the Eurocode 2 steel material model is not appropriate for structural fire engineering analysis, and a creep free steel material model is proposed for general application.

creep free analysis of structures with the Eurocode 2 material model for steel is possible and that creep free analysis should be used to evaluate the behaviour of steel structures exposed to fire, as it is the most realistic approach.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a creep free analysis is possible with the Eurocode 4 steel material model, and that creep free analysis can reveal the influence of inherent implicit creep in the EuroCode 4 steel material.
the creep free analysis is a useful tool for the structural engineer, which can be employed to reveal the influence and effect of implicit creep.
the creep free analysis of steel structures should not be neglected in structural fire engineering.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the creep free material model can be used to investigate the behaviour of structural steel members in fire.
the Eurocode 4 creep model should be used in the analysis of steel structures exposed to fire.
